name: angelia-gateway
description: Turn the coding agent CLI you already know into the brain of your personal assistants, on WhatsApp and Telegram. One chat, one folder, one session.
_files: Everything an installed copy needs, and nothing else. Without this list npm ships the whole tree - src, tests, docs, plan.md - and `dist/` is only included because no list and no .npmignore exist, so the first .npmignore anyone adds silently removes the very files `bin` points at. Source maps are left out on purpose: they point into `src/`, which an installed copy does not have.

scripts._prepare: Runs after a bare `npm install`, after `npm link`, and when this package is installed straight from git. Without it dist/ does not exist and the `angelia` command points at nothing.
scripts._test: The slow group (a real pack and a global install into an empty prefix) gets its own limit: node applies --test-timeout to the file as a whole, and a cold machine needs minutes for it.
scripts.test: tsc --noEmit && node --test --import tsx --test-timeout=20000 tests/*.test.ts tests/voice/*.test.ts && node --test --import tsx --test-timeout=600000 tests/slow/*.test.ts

_bundleDependencies: All of them: the tarball carries every runtime dependency at the version package-lock.json locked, so an install resolves nothing from the registry on the day. npm ignores a shrinkwrap in a tarball installed by path (measured, npm 11.17), so a lock file alone would not do this. Baileys must be bundled anyway: it is a vendored build of a fork.
